card.name: Digits just before mg units
card.fires_on: Digits or punctuation inside a dose amount, right before the unit mg, gram or kg is written. Seen in dosing text, tables and concentrations.

modes.label: Last digit of a dose
modes.description: A digit that ends or sits inside a number, with mg or mg/mL coming next.
modes.example: Adults: The recommended dosage of RINVOQ is 1<<5>> mg once daily.

modes.label: Dose hyphen or bracket
modes.description: A joining mark just before mg, as in mg-to-mg or a concentration heading.
modes.example: Inappropriate switching on a mg<<-to>>-mg basis from SKELAXIN

modes.label: Digit in weight or table
modes.description: A digit in a weight band or dosing table, followed by a weight or dose unit.
modes.example: Pediatric Weight (2 Years of Age and older) Recommended Dosage 1<<0>> kg (22 lbs) to less

card.writes: It promotes mass units like mg and gram and suppresses unrelated unit-like tokens such as Newton.
card.plain: It fires on the number just before a milligram or gram unit and prepares the text to write that unit.
